Fn::Join:
# Contain a Bedrock AgentCore runtime

Attaches the containment policy to the execution role. Every AWS call made with the role is then denied, except log writes to the runtime's own log groups. Running sessions fail at their next AWS call, as do new sessions, and credentials copied out of a session are denied too. It stops neither callers nor session billing.

* Runtime:

AutomationAssumeRole.description: Role the automation runs as. Defaults to the module-created contain automation role.

SessionIds.description: (Optional) IDs of running sessions to stop once the policy is attached.

Approvers.description: (Optional) IAM principal ARNs, any one of whom must approve before the policy is attached. Leave empty to contain immediately.

inputs.Script:
"""
`contain` and `release` runbook step: resolves the execution role's name from its ARN.

The IAM calls the runbooks make take a role name, but a referenced role's ARN can be
a dynamic reference (`roleArn: ssm:/...`) that resolves only at deploy, so the name
cannot be derived at synth. A role name is the last segment of the ARN's path.
"""


def handler(events: dict, _context: object) -> dict:
    role_arn = str(events.get("RoleArn") or "")
    parts = role_arn.split(":", 5)
    resource = parts[5] if len(parts) == 6 and parts[2] == "iam" else ""
    if not resource.startswith("role/"):
        raise ValueError(f"{role_arn!r} is not an IAM role ARN, so the containment runbooks cannot act on it.")
    return {"RoleName": resource.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]}

"""
`contain` runbook step: reports whether the execution named any approvers.

aws:branch compares only strings, numbers and booleans, so it cannot test the
`Approvers` StringList for emptiness itself. This step turns it into a boolean
the branch can evaluate.
"""


def handler(events: dict, _context: object) -> dict:
    approvers = [a for a in events.get("Approvers") or [] if isinstance(a, str) and a.strip()]
    return {"HasApprovers": bool(approvers)}

Fn::Join: Approve containment of Bedrock AgentCore runtime
. Every AWS call made with its execution role will be denied until release.

inputs.Script:
"""
`contain` runbook step: tags the execution role with the containment time.

The `release` runbook's gate is measured from this tag, so the value must be
written in the format release_gate.py parses (TIMESTAMP_FORMAT, UTC). Running
`contain` again on a contained role moves the tag forward, which only lengthens
the gate.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timezone

import boto3

TIMESTAMP_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"


def handler(events: dict, _context: object) -> dict:
    contained_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(TIMESTAMP_FORMAT)
    boto3.client("iam").tag_role(
        RoleName=events["RoleName"],
        Tags=[{"Key": events["TagKey"], "Value": contained_at}],
    )
    return {"ContainedAt": contained_at}

Fn::Join:
# Release a contained Bedrock AgentCore runtime

Detaches the containment policy from the execution role and removes the containment tag. Refuses until the release gate has passed: the containment time, plus the runtime's maxLifetime (8 hours), plus the role's MaxSessionDuration. Until then, a session that was running at containment may still hold credentials that would work again on release. Sessions started or resumed while contained are not covered, so block new invocations before relying on the gate.

* Runtime:

AutomationAssumeRole.description: Role the automation runs as. Defaults to the module-created release automation role.

Force.description: Skips the release gate. Use only after stopping the live sessions by ID and revoking the role's active sessions.
